text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Wednesday.

LONDON - Stocks closed higher as the market gave an initial welcome to the tax plans and economic forecasts in the early part of Chancellor Gordon Brown's budget. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,751.4, up 23.1 points, or 0.49 percent.

FRANKFURT - Stocks hit record highs as blue chips got a strong boost from the firm dollar, always a plus for a market thronged by export-driven firms. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,854.76, up 34.91 points, or 0.91 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 3,867.53, up 32.69 points, or 0.85 percent.

PARIS - French government threats to tax company profits throttled a fresh stock market surge after high liquidity, a strong dollar and buoyant overseas markets powered stock prices to a new record. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,909.45, down 34.59 points, or 1.17 percent.

ZURICH - Stocks ended slightly above Tuesday's closing levels, but investors held back ahead of the outcome of the U.S. Federal Reserve's two-day meeting ending Tuesday. The Swiss market index closed at 5,674.3, up 19.5 points, or 0.34 percent.
TOKYO - Stocks closed slightly higher after bouncing back from a morning slump. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,196.42, up 20.90 points, or 0.10 percent.
HONG KONG - The stock market was closed again as the country celebrates its return to Chinese rule. The market reopens Thursday.

SYDNEY - The stock market streaked to a record close as enthusiastic investors bid blue chips higher in a broad-based rally. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,745.9, up 24.7 points, or 0.91 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Industrial stocks, unfazed by a lower-than-expected reserves figure, climbed to their fifth consecutive record high, fuelled by gains in heavyweight stock Richemont. The All-Share index closed at 7,416.7, down 3.4 points, or 0.05 percent. The All-Gold index closed at 964.7, down 3.9 points, or 0.4 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,832.5, up 23.8 points, or 0.27 percent.
